question_type: average of three monthly amount-outstanding values from a series named with an elided noun (United States savings notes vs savings bonds 'Sales and Redemptions by Periods')

opus_path.decision: Mapped 'United States ... sales and redemptions ... outstanding' to a 'Sales and Redemptions by Periods' table in a 'UNITED STATES SAVINGS ___' section (bonds SB-x or notes SN-1), with the monthly 'Amount outstanding' column; flagged the missing noun (bonds vs notes) as the main ambiguity; Q3 = Jul/Aug/Sep monthly rows.
Listed the 1982-84 issues: monthly issues through 1982_11 (no 1982_12), then quarterly. Candidates are 1982_10 (table ends at Sept 1982), 1982_11 and the 1983 quarterly issues.
Grepped 'sales and redemptions' in 1982_11 and 1983_03; found SB-1, SB-2, SB-3 and SN-1; 1983_03 has no monthly outstanding table (dead end).
Read both candidate tables: SB-2 splits 'Amount outstanding' into interest-bearing and matured non-interest-bearing; SN-1 has one un-subdivided 'Amount outstanding' column.
Checked later vintages: from 1983_06 the sections merge into SBN-2 (bonds+notes combined), so no separate later notes series exists. Noted an OCR slip in the Oct 1982 SB-2 matured column for Sept.
Cross-checked the notes and bonds monthly values against the independent nonmarketable public-debt table in the 1982_08, 1982_09 and 1982_10 issues; exact match.

Built a four-row candidate table (SN-1; SB-2 interest-bearing; SB-2 interest-bearing + matured; SBN-2 combined) and chose SN-1: the question names one un-qualified 'amount outstanding', which only SN-1 has, and SN-1's section heading plus title match the paraphrase with the least dropped text.
Averaged the three monthly cells at full precision in calc.py, then rounded once to the nearest million.
Reviewer confirmed data and arithmetic; verdict 'uncertain' because of the wording ambiguity, with the savings-bonds reading as the main alternative.

opus_key_moves: Enumerated every table titled 'Sales and Redemptions by Periods' (SB-2, SB-3, SN-1) and put all readings side by side before choosing.

Used a column-structure argument: the question names a single un-qualified 'amount outstanding', which only the savings-notes table has; the savings-bonds table would need a sub-column choice the question never names.
Cross-checked the chosen series against an independent public-debt table.

C019's arithmetic advice is sound, but its 'write a script file' instruction, combined with the Codex apply_patch convention, caused the tooling thrash. C019's trigger 'all series combined' coincides with SB-2's title, but there is no visible evidence that it steered the table choice.

remedies.intervention: Mandatory candidate-table stage (as for none): enumerate every table whose title contains the key phrase, show section headings and column headers, and require an explicit rejection reason for each.

remedies.intervention: A native file-write/calculator tool, so that cards requiring script-based arithmetic do not send the actor into shell-quoting workarounds.

right_arms_note: prompt was right through memory: a lesson from an earlier savings-notes question named SN-1 and its location, so the arm went straight there and never had to resolve the ambiguity. The wrong arms had SN-1's title in their own grep output but never opened it.
text_vs_mechanism: The text that helped was not a rule but a series-location fact that happened to be in the prompt arm's context (memory delivered as text). A general disambiguation instruction is unlikely to be enough on its own: the cards arm considered notes and dismissed them in one line. What generalizes is a forced candidate-table comparison (CONTROL) or a table-catalog tool, plus a retrieval-indexed series memory (STATE) that gives the prompt arm's advantage without a 184 KB context.
notes: Opus's own reviewer rated this 'uncertain'; the official answer follows the savings-notes reading. The two wrong arms also split on vintage for the bonds matured cell: none kept the Oct 1982 cell, which is an OCR slip, while cards took the Nov revision. A CHECK comparing a cell across adjacent printings would flag such OCR slips in general. Opus's tie-breaker (prefer the table whose column needs no unnamed sub-column choice) is a reusable document-QA heuristic.
